diagram_math_checks.result: Six cyclic vertices are exactly (1,0),(1/2,sqrt(3)/2),(-1/2,sqrt(3)/2),(-1,0),(-1/2,-sqrt(3)/2),(1/2,-sqrt(3)/2); o=(0,0). TikZ uses symbolic sqrt(3)/2, not inferred coordinates. Step 1.1 enumerates precisely these six sides. Explicit last segment v5--v0 closes the hexagon.

Step 3.1 defines s(x,y)=(x/2+cy,cx-y/2), t(x,y)=(x/2-cy,-cx-y/2), c=sqrt(3)/2, with s^2=t^2=(st)^3=1. Substitution sends v0 under 1,s,st,sts,ts,t to v0,v1,v2,v3,v4,v5 respectively, exactly the caption cyclic order. Right multiplication along the cycle alternates s,t,s,t,s,t. No extra generator or directed-edge claim is made.

The boundary graph has edges 01,12,23,34,45,50; six vertices and six undirected edges, each vertex degree 2. Independent BFS on this adjacency returned distances from v0 to v1,v2,v3 equal to 1,2,3. Step 4.1 independently proves minimality via index increments modulo 6. The highlighted upper arc has exactly those successive lengths. The centre and dashed segments are explicitly excluded from graph edges.

From the displayed coordinates, squared distances from v0 to v1,v2,v3 are 1/4+3/4=1, 9/4+3/4=3, and 4. All boundary side squared lengths are 1. Step 2.1 identifies d with Euclidean distance on the convex single cell and proves straight segments geodesic; steps 3.2 and 4.1 give exact comparison pairs (1,1),(sqrt(3),2),(2,3). Diameter v0-v3 passes through o and has length 2. No barycentric edges or subdivision claims are drawn.
